page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose server instance configured with 1 vCPU and 4 GB of RAM. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. The CPU allocation is dedicated, providing 1 physical core and 1 thread per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks highlight a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2647.38. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression operate at average speeds of 25.79 GB/sec and 11.3 GB/sec respectively. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing scores all falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides dedicated AMD EPYC CPU resources without the resource-sharing overhead of burstable instances, making it a stable choice for low-demand applications. It is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic text processing, single-threaded scripts, small-scale development environments, and low-traffic web serving.
